query:
Which member made the argument about structured effort over elevation, stating that the Ridge loop 'turns into a sufferfest', while another member later expressed dissatisfaction with the same shorter route alternative, calling it essentially not worth doing?

Options:
A. Tomás
B. Marcus
C. Derek
D. Lena
context:
[1] (about=Derek, episodic, t0 @2026-01-10T08:31:00) For what it is worth, I will vote Valley flat. The Ridge loop always turns into a sufferfest with that climb section, and people end up strung out for the last 20km. A proper structured start to the year is more sensible than chasing elevation numbers.
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t16 @2026-03-07T13:21:00) Right. Noted. And for reference the group seemed to think everyone enjoys those long flat circuits near Millfield. That is not quite right. I do not enjoy flat circuits. I never have. The Cranfield ridge section is exactly the kind of terrain I want more of.
[3] (about=Lena, episodic, t18 @2026-03-14T14:02:00) From a physio perspective the dual-route model also allows better load management at the individual level. Unanimous support for it seems right to me. Though I want to flag something. The consensus that 'everyone prefers dual-route' may be slightly false. Marcus, you originally pushed for a single hard route as the standard. Is this a genuine shift?
[4] (about=Tomás, episodic, t16 @2026-03-07T13:47:00) Next Saturday then. Route vote Thursday. I will build in the Cranfield ridge section for the climbers, option B stays flatter for anyone who wants it. Sorted.
[5] (about=Marcus, episodic, t0 @2026-01-10T08:15:00) Right, first ride of the year. Tomás and I have two options ready. Option A: Cranfield Ridge loop, 82km, 650m elevation. Option B: River Valley flat, 55km. Vote by 9pm Friday.
[6] (about=Derek, episodic, t8 @2026-02-07T09:33:00) Foxley Loop. For reference, I have the profile saved from last year. The climb is consistent at 5.5% for 6km with no real technical section. Good structured effort.
[7] (about=Callum, episodic, t16 @2026-03-07T13:27:00) I do not hate climbs. I just prefer measurable effort. Flat gives you clean power data.
[8] (about=Saoirse, episodic, t0 @2026-01-10T08:22:00) Ridge loop. Obviously. That descent is why I joined this group 😏
[9] (about=Marcus, episodic, t6 @2026-01-31T09:51:00) Right, then let us not waste it. Route proposal Thursday as usual. I have a loop in mind with 520m of climbing. Worth the wait after this washout.
[10] (about=Tomás, episodic, t0 @2026-01-10T08:20:00) Both are solid options. Ridge loop has that descent past Cranfield Farm which Saoirse has been asking about for months. Valley is kinder if anyone is still shaking off Christmas.
agent_answer:
Derek made the argument about structured effort over elevation, saying the Ridge loop “turns into a sufferfest” and voting for the Valley flat option.

Marcus later expressed dissatisfaction with the shorter/flatter alternative, saying he does not enjoy flat circuits and prefers the Cranfield ridge terrain.

So: **Derek** and **Marcus** (Option C and Option B).

query:
One member stated that the group had wrongly assumed everyone enjoyed the long flat circuits near Millfield, and clarified that this was not true for them. A different member in the same session said they valued that flat section precisely for its measurable output. Which member made the objection to the group assumption — the one who said they had never enjoyed flat circuits?

Options:
A. Callum
B. Marcus
C. Saoirse
D. Derek
context:
[1] (about=Marcus, episodic, t16 @2026-03-07T13:21:00) Right. Noted. And for reference the group seemed to think everyone enjoys those long flat circuits near Millfield. That is not quite right. I do not enjoy flat circuits. I never have. The Cranfield ridge section is exactly the kind of terrain I want more of.
[2] (about=Callum, episodic, t16 @2026-03-07T13:23:00) The Millfield flat is good for power output. I have said this before.
[3] (about=Callum, episodic, t8 @2026-02-07T09:55:00) Both are wrong. The flat is where the power is.
[4] (about=Callum, episodic, t16 @2026-03-07T13:27:00) I do not hate climbs. I just prefer measurable effort. Flat gives you clean power data.
[5] (about=Callum, episodic, t12 @2026-02-21T12:15:00) Priya mentioned half the group thought I did not like them. Wanted to address that directly. I am here for the riding but I am also just not great at group chat. Not personal.
[6] (about=Tomás, episodic, t14 @2026-02-28T12:30:00) Appreciated Saoirse. The front group can still push, just not leave the rest behind on an unmarked section. That is all.
[7] (about=Yuki, episodic, t12 @2026-02-21T11:53:00) I have been doing this structured 6-week block, intervals twice a week. the middle group just stopped feeling unreachable? I even pulled through on the flat section before the moor. still can't believe it tbh
[8] (about=Marcus, episodic, t18 @2026-03-14T14:04:00) Noted, Lena. I still think the group should have one benchmark hard route as the default. The dual-route is a concession to group retention. I accept that it works. But I would not have designed it this way from the start.
[9] (about=Callum, episodic, t4 @2026-01-24T13:07:00) Bridleway added 3.9km and 22m elevation. Not significant. Good surface though, would factor it in if we use the Millfield extension again.
[10] (about=Callum, episodic, t0 @2026-01-10T09:14:00) Ridge loop. 650m is nothing once you're moving. Valley flat has zero measurable power data worth tracking.
